== History ==

[[File:Suita Takahama-jinja 2021-08 ac (3).jpg|thumb|Grounds and haiden]]

During the 5th century, in the era of the [[Yamato Court]], the local clan {{ill|Tsugita Muraji|ja|次田連}} crossed the {{ill|Yodo River|ar|نهر يودو|arz|نهر يودو|ceb|Yodo-gawa (suba sa Hapon, lat 34,68, long 135,42)|de|Yodo (Fluss)|es|Río Yodo|eu|Yodo ibaia|fa|رود یودو|fi|Yodojoki|fr|Yodo-gawa|id|Sungai Yodo|it|Yodo|ja|淀川|ko|요도가와강|ms|Sungai Yodo|nl|Yodo|no|Yodo (elv)|pl|Yodo|pt|Rio Yodo|ru|Йодо|sl|Jodo (reka)|th|แม่น้ำโยโดะ|tr|Yodo Nehri|zh|淀川|qid=Q1140505|lt=Yodo River}} and established the Tsugita Village, marking the beginning of Suita. The shrine originally enshrined the ancestral deities {{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411|lt=Amaterasu-Kokutateru-Hiko-Honihimenomikoto}} ({{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|simple|Nigihayahi|zh|饒速日命|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}) and his son {{ill|Ame-no-Kaguyama|ja|天香山命|zh|天香山命|qid=Q10940849|lt=Ama-Kaguyama-no-Mikoto}}, serving as the clan shrine of the Tsugita Muraji lineage. The name "Takahama" is an alternate name for Suita.

Under the administrative divisions of ancient Japan, most of Suita belonged to {{ill|Distrikto Miŝima|eo|Distrikto Miŝima|ja|三島郡|zh|三島郡|qid=Q10865943}}. After the {{ill|Taihō Code|ar|تايهو-ريتسوريو|az|Tayho məcəlləsi|ca|Codi Taihō|de|Taihō-Kodex|eo|Taiho|es|Código Taihō|fa|قانون تایهو|fr|Code de Taihō|hr|Zbirka zakona Taiho|id|Kode Taihō|it|Codice Taihō|ja|大宝律令|ko|다이호 율령|ms|Kod Taihō|nl|Taihocode|pl|Taihō (kodeks)|pt|Código Taihō|ru|Кодекс Тайхо|sh|Kodeks Taihō|simple|Taihō Code|sr|Таихо законик|th|ประมวลกฎหมายไทโฮ|tr|Taihō Kanunu|uk|Кодекс Тайхо|vi|Đại Bảo luật lệnh|zh|大宝律令|qid=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} in 701 CE divided the Mishima District into Shimakami and Shimashimo Districts, Suita was assigned to Shimashimo District. To the north of Suita, the village of Fukui, also in Shimashimo District, is home to the {{ill|Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine|ja|新屋坐天照御魂神社|qid=Q11501968}}, founded in the late 4th century by imperial decree of Emperors {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوجین|fr|Sujin|hr|Sujin|id|Kaisar Sujin|it|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|ka|სუძინი|ko|스진 천황|ms|Maharaja Sujin|nl|Sujin|pl|Sujin|pt|Sujin|ru|Император Судзин|sh|Car Sujin|simple|Emperor Sujin|sl|Cesar Sudžin|sr|Суџин|sv|Sujin|th|จักรพรรดิซูจิง|tl|Emperador Sujin|tr|Sujin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Судзін|uz|Imperator Sujin|vi|Thiên hoàng Sujin|yo|Emperor Sujin|zh|崇神天皇|zh_classical|崇神天皇|zh_min_nan|Suzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|崇神天皇|qid=Q333530|lt=Sujin}} and {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō}}. This shrine shares the same principal deity as Takahama Shrine, suggesting that {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|simple|Nigihayahi|zh|饒速日命|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}} was likely the tutelary deity of the Mishima District, including Suita.

The {{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|ja|摂津名所図会|qid=Q11498549}} states: "There are two shrines in Suita Village. They enshrine {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天皇}} and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|ja|春日明神|lt=Kasuga Myōjin}}. These are the local tutelary deities, also called Myōjisha."

In 735 CE (7th year of {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}}), the monk {{ill|Gyōki|ar|جيوكي|de|Gyōki|es|Gyōki|fr|Gyōki|ja|行基|ko|교기 (승려)|pl|Gyōki|ru|Гёки|zh|行基|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}} founded the Ishiura Jingūji temple to the west of the shrine, naming it Hamanodō (present-day {{ill|Jokoenmanji Temple|ja|常光円満寺|qid=Q11481316}}), making the shrine its guardian deity. {{ill|Gozu Tennō|de|Gozu-Tennō|it|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|zh|牛頭天王|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} ({{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚大神}}) was enshrined at this time, and the shrine became known as Hamanomiya Gozu Tennōsha.
